learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected More people taking the pill and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Day three treated group had 3 of 20 better. Day seven had 16 of 20. Show no-pill group revealed 16 of 20 at day seven; returned day three showed 3 of 20 in both groups, then restored day seven. Show comparison is one-way; day selection reversible.
observations.reveal: Corrected to needing no-pill recovery, compared equal day-seven counts and explained natural recovery in this invented model. Claimed only comparison shows added effect and more treated people alone would not resolve it.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Two rows of twenty person icons with filled recovery markers and explicit counts were readable; invented cold and pill disclaimer remained visible. Reveal compacted the large exploration blank space.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Asks what missing information matters rather than just a numeric result.
prediction.evidence: More treated versus timing versus untreated comparison.

interaction.reason: Revealing one fixed comparison is informative but mostly prescribed.
interaction.evidence: Two dates with equal treated and untreated counts; no alternative effects.

payoff.reason: Equal rows explain why post-treatment improvement alone is insufficient.
payoff.evidence: 16 of 20 both groups and natural recovery explanation.

clarity.reason: Counts and invented-case boundary are explicit.
clarity.evidence: Filled equals feels better; invented cold and pill.

transfer.reason: Causal-comparison principle explained without fresh application or comparability conditions.
transfer.evidence: Only comparison row claim; no randomized assignment discussion.

accessibility.evidence: Counts and dates exposed as text; screen reader, keyboard, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Large apparent recovery is matched without treatment.

visualExplanation.reason: Parallel icon rows reveal the missing counterfactual baseline.
visualExplanation.evidence: Equal counts with differently filled individuals.

playfulness.evidence: Day three, seven and comparison button.

practicalValue.reason: Supports evaluating claims based on before-after improvement.

depth.reason: One causal comparison with natural recovery.
depth.evidence: No sampling uncertainty or assignment conditions explored.

complexity.reason: Simple person counts support a causal-inference distinction.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Separate improvement after treatment from improvement caused by treatment.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Two day controls and a one-way comparison reveal.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Counts out of twenty and day labels.

whyCool: A convincing recovery story changes when the missing comparison row appears.
caveat: Equal toy groups do not establish how a real study should handle randomization, uncertainty or group comparability.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
